editorial:
Imagine you are back in 1970, where beauty pageants were the biggest deal on TV and women were expected to just smile and look pretty. You get to follow a group of bold, rebellious women who are tired of these outdated rules. They decide to crash the Miss World competition in London to make a loud statement about women's rights. The movie feels like a heist film but with a political twist, blending funny moments with a lot of tension as the ladies plan their big move. You will find yourself rooting for the underdogs as they try to sneak into the theater and throw things on stage to stop the show.

The acting is great, especially the way it shows the friendship and anger of the protesters. The pacing is quick, so you will not get bored, though some of the side plots feel a bit rushed. If you like stories about people standing up for what is right, you will love this. For the best experience, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the cool vintage costumes. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move for the crisp picture quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a huge shock when a contestant from Puerto Rico wins the crown instead of a white woman. This flips the script on the beauty standards of the time. The protesters realize that while their disruption got attention, the actual result of the pageant was even more revolutionary. It wraps up by showing how this one night helped launch the women's liberation movement into the global spotlight, changing how the world viewed beauty forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about rebellion and social change.
